input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: Section 10(a) gives us a broad Kubient-side defence and indemnity for third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, the Creative served by the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors. IP infringement is squarely covered: Kubient warrants in §9(b)(i) that the Service and deliverables do not infringe or misappropriate any third-party IP, privacy or publicity rights, and 10(a)(iv) indemnifies breach of that warranty, in addition to the general "arising out of the Services / Auction Platform" trigger. Vendor misconduct is covered by 10(a)(v). Section 11 supplies standard procedure (prompt notice that is not a condition to recovery, indemnifying-party control with no liability-admitting settlement absent our consent, cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost), and §7(a) carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages exclusion; there is no monetary liability cap applied to the indemnity, so no super-cap concern arises. This meets the preferred position. Noted but not flagged: AP's reciprocal indemnity in 10(b) is somewhat wider than the preferred "Customer content and Customer's breach of law" formulation (it also picks up AP's breach of any representation or warranty and acts/omissions of AP and its contractors), and the Creative limb of Kubient's indemnity is knowledge-qualified. These are mirror-image, minor sub-elements against an otherwise strong vendor indemnity and do not warrant a redline.
